chunks: Some of our companions, from Ibn Jumhur, from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim, from Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'fur, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I happen to be in the thickets/marshes, and various birds come over me. What can I eat from them?' He said: 'Eat what flaps its wings, and do not eat what glides (with outstretched wings).' I said: 'I am brought (birds) that are already slaughtered.' He said: 'Eat what had a craw (gizzard).'

key_terms.الْآجَامِ: Thickets, reed beds, marshes — dense vegetated areas near water
key_terms.دَفَّ: Flapping of wings — the primary mode of flight in halal birds
key_terms.صَفَّ: Soaring/gliding with outstretched wings — characteristic of birds of prey
key_terms.قَانِصَةٌ: Craw/gizzard — the muscular stomach present in permissible birds

ai.seo_question: What are the Islamic criteria for identifying permissible birds to eat according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes two practical criteria for determining the permissibility of birds as food. The first criterion applies to live birds: only those that primarily flap their wings (daf') are permissible, while those that primarily soar or glide (saff) are forbidden — a distinction that excludes birds of prey such as eagles and hawks. The second criterion applies when the bird's type is unknown after slaughter: permissibility is confirmed by the presence of a craw (qaanisa/gizzard), which is characteristic of seed-eating birds but absent in predatory birds. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential position attributed to the Imams of the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.hubeali: One of our companions, from Ibn jamhour, from Muhammad Bin Al Qasim, form Abdullah Bin Abu Yafour who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘I happened to be in the bushes, so there was an interchange of different birds upon me. So what can I eat from these?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Eat what flaps (its wings), and do not eat what arrays (its wings)’. So I said, ‘I am brought with (birds) as slaughtered’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said ‘Eat what had a craw for it’.
en.sarwar: 6. Certain persons of our people have narrated from ibn Jumhur from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim from ‘Abd Allah ibn abu Ya‘fur who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, about birds that I find in wilderness and about which is edible. He (the Imam) said, ‘All birds that flap their wings in flight are edible and all birds that keep their wings straight in flight are not edible.’ ‘What happens if they are brought to me already slaughtered?’ He (the Imam) said, ’Eat whatever has craws.’”
